glossary.text: A grid of rows and columns about one kind of thing (molecules, products, measurements).
What one row represents. Always check it before counting: 'one row = one molecule' and 'one row = one measurement' give very different totals.
The column (or columns) that identify a row uniquely, like chembl_id in molecules. No two rows share it.
A column that points to the primary key of another table, so the two tables can be combined with JOIN.
A saved query that looks like a table but is recalculated each time. Here v_molecule_routes.
The stored result of a view, so it does not have to be recalculated. Here molecule_routes.
An empty cell: the value is unknown or does not apply. NULL is not zero, and COUNT(column) skips it.
Identifier given by the ChEMBL database to molecules (CHEMBL714), targets, assays and documents.
Many drugs are sold as salts (albuterol sulfate). The parent is the active molecule without the counter-ion; properties are compared on the parent.
A one-line text code for a chemical structure, readable by chemistry software.
The concentration of a compound that reduces the enzyme activity by half. Lower IC50 = more potent.
The inhibition constant, a measure of how tightly a compound binds its target. Lower Ki = tighter binding.
The same values on a log scale: 9 - log10(value in nM). Higher = more potent; +1 = 10 times more potent.
A result reported only as a limit, like '> 10,000 nM'. It is not an exact measurement, so it is excluded from potency estimates.
How much a molecule prefers an oily phase to water. Lipophilic drugs (high logP) tend to stay longer in membranes and tissues.
Polar surface area: the part of the molecular surface made by oxygen, nitrogen and their hydrogens. High PSA = more polar, crosses membranes less easily.
Lipinski's guideline for oral absorption: MW ≤ 500, logP ≤ 5, at most 5 H-bond donors and 10 acceptors.
WHO classification of drugs by organ system and therapeutic use, in five levels (R → R03 → R03A → R03AC → R03AC02).
Types of FDA application: new drug, abbreviated (generic) new drug, biologics license.
How a product enters the body: inhalation, oral, intravenous...

tables.name: dataset_info
tables.purpose: Key-value list that records the source releases, the download time of every raw file and its SHA-256 fingerprint.
tables.use_for: Citing the data version in a report, or checking that two people analysed the same input files.
tables.watch_out: Values are stored as text, including dates.

columns.name: key
columns.meaning: Name of the fact, e.g. chembl_release, built_at, sha256:<file>, retrieved_at:<file>.

columns.name: value
columns.meaning: Value of the fact, stored as text.

tables.name: molecules
tables.purpose: Every ChEMBL molecule in the project: the 4,225 approved drugs plus the 7,326 compounds tested on PDE4, with structure and computed physicochemical properties.
tables.grain: one ChEMBL molecule (a salt and its parent are separate rows)
tables.use_for: Looking up names, structures and properties; most other tables join here through a ChEMBL ID.
tables.watch_out: Salt forms (e.g. albuterol sulfate) are separate rows that point to their parent through parent_chembl_id: compare properties on the parent. 95 research compounds point to a parent that was not downloaded. The ChemAxon columns (cx_*, molecular_species) are empty because the ChEMBL 37 API does not return them.
tables.example:
SELECT chembl_id, pref_name, mw_freebase, alogp, psa, hbd, hba
FROM molecules
WHERE max_phase = 4 AND molecule_type = 'Small molecule'
ORDER BY mw_freebase DESC
LIMIT 20;

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the molecule, e.g. CHEMBL714 for albuterol. Stable across ChEMBL releases.

columns.name: pref_name
columns.meaning: Preferred name in ChEMBL, usually the international non-proprietary name (INN) in capitals. Empty for most research compounds.

columns.name: molecule_type
columns.meaning: Kind of molecule: Small molecule, Protein, Antibody, Oligonucleotide, Unknown... Empty for many research compounds, where ChEMBL does not set it.

columns.name: max_phase
columns.meaning: Highest clinical phase reached: 4 = approved, 1-3 = clinical trials, empty = research only.

columns.name: first_approval
columns.meaning: Year of the first approval of the molecule, by any route and in any country recorded by ChEMBL.

columns.name: oral
columns.meaning: ChEMBL flag: 1 if the drug has an oral product. ChEMBL has no inhalation flag, which is why FDA routes are used.

columns.name: parenteral
columns.meaning: ChEMBL flag: 1 if the drug has an injectable (parenteral) product.

columns.name: topical
columns.meaning: ChEMBL flag: 1 if the drug has a topical product (skin, eye...).

columns.name: prodrug
columns.meaning: 1 if the molecule is a prodrug: inactive until the body converts it (e.g. ciclesonide).

columns.name: natural_product
columns.meaning: 1 if the molecule is a natural product or derived from one.

columns.name: parent_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL ID of the parent molecule. For a salt it points to the free base or acid; for a parent it points to itself.

columns.name: canonical_smiles
columns.meaning: Chemical structure written as a SMILES string, one line of text that a program like RDKit can turn back into the molecule.

columns.name: standard_inchi_key
columns.meaning: InChIKey: a 27-character fingerprint of the structure, useful to match the same molecule across databases.

columns.name: full_molformula
columns.meaning: Molecular formula including any salt, e.g. C13H21NO3.

columns.name: mw_freebase
columns.meaning: Molecular weight of the parent molecule without its salt.

columns.name: full_mwt
columns.meaning: Molecular weight including the salt or counter-ion.

columns.name: alogp
columns.meaning: Calculated octanol-water partition coefficient (Crippen ALogP): how much the molecule prefers fat to water. Higher = more lipophilic.

columns.name: cx_logp
columns.meaning: ChemAxon logP. Always empty: the ChEMBL 37 API does not return ChemAxon descriptors.

columns.name: cx_logd
columns.meaning: ChemAxon logD at pH 7.4. Always empty for the same reason.

columns.name: psa
columns.meaning: Polar surface area: the surface belonging to oxygen, nitrogen and their hydrogens. A proxy for polarity and for how easily a molecule crosses membranes.

columns.name: hba
columns.meaning: Number of hydrogen-bond acceptors (mainly O and N atoms). Lipinski's rule of five expects at most 10.

columns.name: hbd
columns.meaning: Number of hydrogen-bond donors (OH and NH groups). Lipinski's rule of five expects at most 5.

columns.name: rtb
columns.meaning: Number of rotatable bonds: single bonds the molecule can twist around. A measure of flexibility.

columns.name: aromatic_rings
columns.meaning: Number of aromatic rings, such as benzene or pyridine rings.

columns.name: heavy_atoms
columns.meaning: Number of non-hydrogen atoms. A size measure used for ligand efficiency.

columns.name: num_ro5_violations
columns.meaning: How many of Lipinski's four rules the molecule breaks (MW ≤ 500, logP ≤ 5, HBD ≤ 5, HBA ≤ 10).

columns.name: qed_weighted
columns.meaning: Quantitative estimate of drug-likeness: one score that combines eight properties. 1 = very typical oral drug, 0 = very unusual.

columns.name: cx_most_apka
columns.meaning: ChemAxon most acidic pKa. Always empty for the same reason.

columns.name: cx_most_bpka
columns.meaning: ChemAxon most basic pKa. Always empty for the same reason.

columns.name: molecular_species
columns.meaning: ChemAxon charge class (ACID, BASE, NEUTRAL, ZWITTERION). Always empty for the same reason.

columns.name: np_likeness_score
columns.meaning: How much the structure resembles natural products. Positive = natural-product-like.

columns.name: source_set
columns.meaning: Why the molecule is in the project: 'approved', 'pde4_tested', or 'approved+pde4_tested'.

tables.name: molecule_synonyms
tables.purpose: Alternative names of the approved drugs: international (INN), US (USAN) and British (BAN) names, trade names and research codes.
tables.use_for: Finding a drug by any of its names, and matching FDA ingredient names to ChEMBL.
tables.watch_out: Only approved drugs have synonyms here. The same name can appear with several syn_type values.
tables.example:
SELECT m.pref_name, s.synonym, s.syn_type
FROM molecule_synonyms AS s
JOIN molecules AS m ON m.chembl_id = s.chembl_id
WHERE s.synonym LIKE 'ALBUTEROL%';

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the molecule, e.g. CHEMBL714 for albuterol. Stable across ChEMBL releases.

columns.name: synonym
columns.meaning: One alternative name of the molecule.

columns.name: syn_type
columns.meaning: Source or kind of name: INN (international), USAN (US), BAN (British), JAN (Japanese), FDA, TRADE_NAME, RESEARCH_CODE, OTHER...

tables.name: atc_classes
tables.purpose: The WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification: a five-level tree from the organ system down to the single substance.
tables.grain: one ATC level-5 code (one substance in one therapeutic use)
tables.use_for: Grouping drugs by therapeutic area, e.g. R03 = drugs for obstructive airway diseases.
tables.watch_out: A molecule can have several ATC codes (one per use), so joining through molecule_atc can multiply rows.
tables.example:
SELECT level2, level2_description, COUNT(*) AS substances
FROM atc_classes
WHERE level1 = 'R'
GROUP BY level2, level2_description;

columns.name: level5
columns.meaning: ATC level-5 code: one chemical substance in one therapeutic use, e.g. R03AC02 = salbutamol as a selective beta-2 agonist.

columns.name: who_name
columns.meaning: WHO name of the substance for this code.

columns.name: level1
columns.meaning: ATC level 1 (one letter): anatomical main group, e.g. R = respiratory system.

columns.name: level1_description
columns.meaning: Name of the level-1 group.

columns.name: level2
columns.meaning: ATC level 2 (letter + 2 digits): therapeutic subgroup, e.g. R03 = drugs for obstructive airway diseases.

columns.name: level2_description
columns.meaning: Name of the level-2 group.

columns.name: level3
columns.meaning: ATC level 3: pharmacological subgroup, e.g. R03A = adrenergics, inhalants.

columns.name: level3_description
columns.meaning: Name of the level-3 group.
examples: DRUGS FOR PEPTIC ULCER AND GASTRO-OESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE (GORD)

columns.name: level4
columns.meaning: ATC level 4: chemical subgroup, e.g. R03AC = selective beta-2-adrenoreceptor agonists.

columns.name: level4_description
columns.meaning: Name of the level-4 group.
examples: Antiinfectives and antiseptics for local oral treatment

tables.name: molecule_atc
tables.purpose: Bridge table that assigns ATC codes to approved molecules.
tables.grain: one ATC code of one molecule
tables.use_for: Answering 'which drugs belong to this class?' or 'which classes does this drug belong to?'.
tables.watch_out: Codes are often stored on the salt form, not on the parent. The cleaned inhalation_dataset.atc_codes already combines both.
tables.example:
SELECT m.pref_name, a.level5, a.who_name, a.level4_description
FROM molecule_atc AS ma
JOIN atc_classes AS a ON a.level5 = ma.level5
JOIN molecules AS m ON m.chembl_id = ma.chembl_id
WHERE a.level3 = 'R03A';

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL ID of the molecule (often the salt form) that carries the code.

columns.name: level5
columns.meaning: The ATC level-5 code. Joins to atc_classes.level5.

tables.name: targets
tables.purpose: The biological targets of the PDE4 activity data: the four human isoforms PDE4A-D and the PDE4 family record.
tables.use_for: Giving readable names to the target IDs in activities.
tables.watch_out: The PROTEIN FAMILY record collects assays that did not specify the isoform.

columns.name: target_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the biological target. Joins to targets.target_chembl_id.

columns.name: pref_name
columns.meaning: Full target name, e.g. 3',5'-cyclic-AMP phosphodiesterase 4B.

columns.name: target_type
columns.meaning: SINGLE PROTEIN or PROTEIN FAMILY.

columns.name: organism
columns.meaning: Species of the target: Homo sapiens for all rows.

tables.name: activities
tables.purpose: Raw bioactivity measurements (IC50 and Ki) of compounds on PDE4, both as written in the paper and as standardised by ChEMBL.
tables.grain: one measurement reported in one paper
tables.use_for: Auditing the raw data and understanding what the cleaning removed. For analysis, use activities_clean.
tables.watch_out: Contains censored values ('>' or '<'), mixed published units and measurements flagged by ChEMBL curators. A lower IC50 means a more potent compound.
tables.example:
SELECT standard_relation, standard_units, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM activities
GROUP BY standard_relation, standard_units
ORDER BY n DESC;

columns.name: activity_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the single measurement.

columns.name: molecule_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the tested molecule. Joins to molecules.chembl_id.

columns.name: target_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the biological target. Joins to targets.target_chembl_id.

columns.name: assay_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the experiment (assay) in which the value was measured.

columns.name: assay_type
columns.meaning: Kind of experiment: B = binding (does it bind the target?), F = functional (does it change the target's activity in a cell or tissue?).

columns.name: document_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the publication or patent that reported the value.

columns.name: document_year
columns.meaning: Year of the publication or patent.

columns.name: standard_type
columns.meaning: Type of measurement: IC50 (concentration that halves the enzyme activity) or Ki (inhibition constant, a measure of binding strength).

columns.name: standard_relation
columns.meaning: Relation of the value: '=' exact, '<' or '>' only a limit (a censored value), empty if not given.

columns.name: standard_value
columns.meaning: Measured value after ChEMBL standardisation. For IC50 and Ki a lower value means a more potent compound.

columns.name: standard_units
columns.meaning: Units after ChEMBL standardisation: nM for almost all rows.

columns.name: pchembl_value
columns.meaning: ChEMBL's potency on a log scale: -log10 of the molar value. 9 = 1 nM, 6 = 1 µM. Only given for clean '=' values.

columns.name: published_type
columns.meaning: Measurement type as written in the paper, before standardisation.

columns.name: published_relation
columns.meaning: Relation as written in the paper.

columns.name: published_value
columns.meaning: Value as written in the paper, in the paper's own unit.

columns.name: published_units
columns.meaning: Unit as written in the paper: nM, uM, mM, %... This mix is why the standardised columns are used.

columns.name: data_validity_comment
columns.meaning: Warning added by ChEMBL curators, e.g. 'Outside typical range' or 'Potential transcription error'. Empty = no warning.

tables.name: fda_applications
tables.purpose: FDA marketing applications: new drugs (NDA), generics (ANDA) and biologics (BLA), with the company that filed them.
tables.use_for: Counting products by sponsor or by application type (the prefix of the number).
tables.watch_out: One application can contain many products (strengths, forms).
tables.example:
SELECT CASE WHEN application_number LIKE 'ANDA%' THEN 'ANDA (generic)'
            WHEN application_number LIKE 'NDA%' THEN 'NDA (new drug)'
            ELSE 'BLA (biologic)' END AS type,
       COUNT(*) AS applications
FROM fda_applications
GROUP BY type;

columns.name: application_number
columns.meaning: FDA application number. The prefix gives the type: NDA (new drug), ANDA (generic), BLA (biologic).

columns.name: sponsor_name
columns.meaning: Company that filed the application.

tables.name: fda_products
tables.purpose: Individual FDA products with brand name, dosage form, route of administration and marketing status. This is where 'inhaled' comes from.
tables.use_for: Finding inhaled, oral or injectable products.
tables.watch_out: The route field is free text: 'INHALATION, ORAL' and 'Inhalation, Oral' mean two routes. Use molecule_routes_clean for a normalised version.
tables.example:
SELECT route, COUNT(*) AS products
FROM fda_products
WHERE UPPER(route) LIKE '%INHAL%'
GROUP BY route;

columns.name: application_number
columns.meaning: FDA application number. The prefix gives the type: NDA (new drug), ANDA (generic), BLA (biologic).

columns.name: product_number
columns.meaning: Number of the product inside its application (one per strength or form).

columns.name: brand_name
columns.meaning: Brand (trade) name of the product, e.g. VENTOLIN HFA.

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.meaning: Physical form of the product, e.g. AEROSOL, METERED; POWDER; TABLET.

columns.name: route
columns.meaning: Route of administration as free text. May contain several routes separated by commas.

columns.name: marketing_status
columns.meaning: Prescription, Over-the-counter, Discontinued, None (tentative approval)...

columns.name: reference_drug
columns.meaning: Yes if the product is a reference listed drug, the one generics are compared with.

tables.name: fda_product_ingredients
tables.purpose: Active ingredients of each FDA product, with the name as written by FDA and the strength.
tables.grain: one active ingredient of one product
tables.use_for: Linking products to molecules through fda_ingredient_map.
tables.watch_out: Ingredient names are often salts (ALBUTEROL SULFATE) and some combinations are written in a single field.
tables.example:
SELECT p.brand_name, i.ingredient_name, i.strength
FROM fda_product_ingredients AS i
JOIN fda_products AS p
  ON p.application_number = i.application_number AND p.product_number = i.product_number
WHERE p.route = 'INHALATION'
LIMIT 20;

columns.name: application_number
columns.meaning: FDA application number. The prefix gives the type: NDA (new drug), ANDA (generic), BLA (biologic).

columns.name: product_number
columns.meaning: Number of the product inside its application (one per strength or form).

columns.name: ingredient_name
columns.meaning: Active ingredient name as written by FDA, in capitals, often including the salt (e.g. ALBUTEROL SULFATE).

columns.name: strength
columns.meaning: Amount of the ingredient as written by FDA, e.g. 0.09MG/INH (per inhalation).

tables.name: fda_ingredient_map
tables.purpose: The bridge between FDA ingredient names and ChEMBL molecules. FDA and ChEMBL share no identifier, so the link is made by name.
tables.use_for: Checking how an FDA name was matched, and how reliable the match is.
tables.watch_out: 7.4% of names stay unmatched (mostly combinations written in one field and recent biologics). match_method tells you how each match was made.

columns.name: ingredient_name
columns.meaning: Active ingredient name as written by FDA, in capitals, often including the salt (e.g. ALBUTEROL SULFATE).

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL molecule whose name or synonym matched (may be a salt). Empty if unmatched.

columns.name: parent_chembl_id
columns.meaning: Parent of the matched molecule: the ID used to compare properties.

columns.name: match_method
columns.meaning: How the match was made: exact (same name), salt_stripped (matched after removing salt words), unmatched.

tables.name: v_molecule_routes
tables.purpose: A view: a saved query that joins products, ingredients and the name map to count products per molecule and route. It is recalculated every time you query it.
tables.grain: one parent molecule and one raw route text
tables.use_for: Reading the join logic. For speed, query molecule_routes instead, which stores the same result.
tables.watch_out: Slow in the browser workbench, because it recomputes a join over 60,000 ingredient rows.
tables.example: SELECT * FROM v_molecule_routes WHERE route = 'INHALATION' LIMIT 20;

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: Parent molecule.

columns.name: route
columns.meaning: Raw FDA route text.

columns.name: n_products
columns.meaning: Number of FDA products with this molecule and this route.

tables.name: molecule_routes
tables.purpose: Stored (materialised) copy of v_molecule_routes, with an index, so the browser can query it fast.
tables.grain: one parent molecule and one raw route text
tables.use_for: Quick route lookups on the raw route text.
tables.watch_out: Uses the raw route text, so 'INHALATION, ORAL' is its own route here. Prefer molecule_routes_clean.
tables.example:
SELECT m.pref_name, r.route, r.n_products
FROM molecule_routes AS r
JOIN molecules AS m ON m.chembl_id = r.chembl_id
WHERE r.route = 'INHALATION'
ORDER BY r.n_products DESC;

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: Parent molecule.

columns.name: route
columns.meaning: Raw FDA route text.

columns.name: n_products
columns.meaning: Number of FDA products with this molecule and this route.

tables.name: molecule_routes_clean
tables.purpose: Routes of administration after cleaning: combined values are split ('INHALATION, ORAL' becomes two rows) and written in upper case.
tables.grain: one parent molecule and one single route
tables.use_for: Any question about which molecules are given by which route.
tables.watch_out: A molecule with both inhaled and oral products has two rows here.
tables.example:
SELECT route, COUNT(*) AS molecules
FROM molecule_routes_clean
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY molecules DESC
LIMIT 10;

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: Parent molecule.

columns.name: route
columns.meaning: One single route in upper case.

columns.name: n_products
columns.meaning: Number of FDA products with this molecule and this route.

tables.name: inhalation_dataset
tables.purpose: The analysis set of the project: approved small molecules split into lung-targeted inhaled drugs and oral drugs, with their properties.
tables.use_for: Comparing inhaled and oral drugs: statistics, PCA, trends over time.
tables.watch_out: The groups are exclusive: a molecule with inhaled products is 'inhaled' even if it also exists orally (also_oral = 1). Gases, diagnostics, CNS-acting inhaled drugs and gut-local oral drugs were removed; see cleaning_log.
tables.example:
SELECT route_group, COUNT(*) AS molecules,
       ROUND(AVG(alogp), 2) AS mean_logp,
       ROUND(AVG(psa), 1) AS mean_psa
FROM inhalation_dataset
GROUP BY route_group;

columns.name: chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the molecule, e.g. CHEMBL714 for albuterol. Stable across ChEMBL releases.

columns.name: pref_name
columns.meaning: Preferred name in ChEMBL, usually the international non-proprietary name (INN) in capitals. Empty for most research compounds.

columns.name: route_group
columns.meaning: Analysis group: 'inhaled' (has at least one inhaled product) or 'oral' (oral products only).

columns.name: also_oral
columns.meaning: 1 if an inhaled molecule also has oral products. Useful to repeat an analysis without them.

columns.name: n_inhaled_products
columns.meaning: Number of FDA inhaled products containing the molecule.

columns.name: n_oral_products
columns.meaning: Number of FDA oral products containing the molecule.

columns.name: atc_codes
columns.meaning: Comma-separated ATC codes of the molecule and of its salt forms.

columns.name: first_approval
columns.meaning: Year of the first approval of the molecule, by any route and in any country recorded by ChEMBL.

columns.name: mw_freebase
columns.meaning: Molecular weight of the parent molecule without its salt.

columns.name: alogp
columns.meaning: Calculated octanol-water partition coefficient (Crippen ALogP): how much the molecule prefers fat to water. Higher = more lipophilic.

columns.name: psa
columns.meaning: Polar surface area: the surface belonging to oxygen, nitrogen and their hydrogens. A proxy for polarity and for how easily a molecule crosses membranes.

columns.name: hbd
columns.meaning: Number of hydrogen-bond donors (OH and NH groups). Lipinski's rule of five expects at most 5.

columns.name: hba
columns.meaning: Number of hydrogen-bond acceptors (mainly O and N atoms). Lipinski's rule of five expects at most 10.

columns.name: rtb
columns.meaning: Number of rotatable bonds: single bonds the molecule can twist around. A measure of flexibility.

columns.name: aromatic_rings
columns.meaning: Number of aromatic rings, such as benzene or pyridine rings.

columns.name: heavy_atoms
columns.meaning: Number of non-hydrogen atoms. A size measure used for ligand efficiency.

columns.name: num_ro5_violations
columns.meaning: How many of Lipinski's four rules the molecule breaks (MW ≤ 500, logP ≤ 5, HBD ≤ 5, HBA ≤ 10).

columns.name: qed_weighted
columns.meaning: Quantitative estimate of drug-likeness: one score that combines eight properties. 1 = very typical oral drug, 0 = very unusual.

tables.name: activities_clean
tables.purpose: PDE4 measurements that passed every cleaning rule, with the potency converted to a logarithmic scale (pIC50 or pKi).
tables.use_for: Potency analysis at the level of single measurements.
tables.watch_out: The same molecule can be measured many times; use activity_potency for one value per molecule and target.
tables.example:
SELECT target_name, standard_type, COUNT(*) AS n,
       ROUND(AVG(p_activity), 2) AS mean_p
FROM activities_clean
GROUP BY target_name, standard_type;

columns.name: activity_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the measurement. Joins to activities.activity_id to see the raw row.

columns.name: molecule_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the tested molecule. Joins to molecules.chembl_id.

columns.name: target_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the biological target. Joins to targets.target_chembl_id.

columns.name: target_name
columns.meaning: Short target name: PDE4A, PDE4B, PDE4C, PDE4D, or 'PDE4 family' when the isoform was not specified.

columns.name: target_type
columns.meaning: SINGLE PROTEIN for one isoform, PROTEIN FAMILY for assays on the family as a whole.

columns.name: assay_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the experiment (assay) in which the value was measured.

columns.name: assay_type
columns.meaning: Kind of experiment: B = binding (does it bind the target?), F = functional (does it change the target's activity in a cell or tissue?).

columns.name: document_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the publication or patent that reported the value.

columns.name: document_year
columns.meaning: Year of the publication or patent.

columns.name: standard_type
columns.meaning: Type of measurement: IC50 (concentration that halves the enzyme activity) or Ki (inhibition constant, a measure of binding strength).

columns.name: standard_value
columns.meaning: Measured value after ChEMBL standardisation. For IC50 and Ki a lower value means a more potent compound.

columns.name: p_activity
columns.meaning: Potency on a log scale computed by the project: 9 - log10(value in nM). pIC50 for IC50 rows, pKi for Ki rows.

columns.name: pchembl_value
columns.meaning: ChEMBL's own log potency, kept to check the project's calculation.

columns.name: pchembl_mismatch
columns.meaning: 1 if p_activity and pchembl_value differ by more than 0.05: a calculation check. 0 for every row in this build.

tables.name: activity_potency
tables.purpose: Repeated measurements collapsed into one median potency per molecule, target and measurement type, with a consistency check.
tables.grain: one molecule on one target with one measurement type
tables.use_for: Ranking compounds by potency and comparing isoforms.
tables.watch_out: inconsistent = 1 marks pairs whose measurements differ more than 10-fold: treat their median with caution.
tables.example:
SELECT m.pref_name, p.target_name, p.p_median, p.n_measurements
FROM activity_potency AS p
JOIN molecules AS m ON m.chembl_id = p.molecule_chembl_id
WHERE m.pref_name IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY p.p_median DESC
LIMIT 20;

columns.name: molecule_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the tested molecule. Joins to molecules.chembl_id.

columns.name: target_chembl_id
columns.meaning: ChEMBL identifier of the biological target. Joins to targets.target_chembl_id.

columns.name: target_name
columns.meaning: Short target name: PDE4A, PDE4B, PDE4C, PDE4D, or 'PDE4 family' when the isoform was not specified.

columns.name: standard_type
columns.meaning: Type of measurement: IC50 (concentration that halves the enzyme activity) or Ki (inhibition constant, a measure of binding strength).

columns.name: p_median
columns.meaning: Median of the log potencies: the summary value to use.

columns.name: p_min
columns.meaning: Lowest log potency among the repeated measurements.

columns.name: p_max
columns.meaning: Highest log potency among the repeated measurements.

columns.name: p_range
columns.meaning: p_max - p_min: how much the repeated measurements disagree. 1 = a 10-fold difference.

columns.name: n_measurements
columns.meaning: Number of clean measurements combined.

columns.name: n_documents
columns.meaning: Number of different publications behind those measurements.

columns.name: inconsistent
columns.meaning: 1 if p_range > 1, i.e. measurements more than 10-fold apart.

tables.name: cleaning_log
tables.purpose: The cleaning ledger: every rule applied, in order, with how many rows it removed or flagged and why.
tables.grain: one cleaning rule (or check) applied to one dataset
tables.use_for: Explaining the data preparation to a reviewer: from the starting rows to the analysed rows, rule by rule.
tables.watch_out: rows_removed counts only the rows removed by that rule; earlier rules already removed others.

columns.name: dataset
columns.meaning: Which cleaned dataset the row belongs to: 'activities' (PDE4 measurements) or 'molecules' (inhaled vs oral analysis set).

columns.name: step
columns.meaning: Order in which the rules were applied within the dataset.

columns.name: rule_id
columns.meaning: Identifier of the cleaning rule: A = activities rules, M = molecules rules, followed by the order. Joins cleaning_log to cleaning_exclusions.

columns.name: kind
columns.meaning: Type of step: input (starting rows), exclude (removes rows), transform (changes values), check (flags rows), aggregate (combines rows).

columns.name: rule
columns.meaning: Short description of what the rule does.
examples: IC50 and Ki measurements on human PDE4 downloaded from ChEMBL

columns.name: reason
columns.meaning: Why the rule is needed.
examples: The data_validity_comment field marks a suspect value (units, transcription, out
Censored values (<, >) only say that potency is above or below a threshold: they

columns.name: unit
columns.meaning: What one row counts at this step: measurements, molecules or molecule-target pairs.

columns.name: rows_before
columns.meaning: Rows before the rule.

columns.name: rows_removed
columns.meaning: Rows removed by this rule only.

columns.name: rows_after
columns.meaning: Rows left after the rule.

columns.name: rows_flagged
columns.meaning: Rows marked by a check but kept.

tables.name: cleaning_exclusions
tables.purpose: Every excluded record with the rule that excluded it: the evidence behind the counts in cleaning_log.
tables.use_for: Answering 'why is this molecule not in my analysis?'.
tables.watch_out: record_id holds an activity_id for dataset 'activities' and a chembl_id for dataset 'molecules'.
tables.example:
SELECT e.rule_id, l.rule, m.pref_name
FROM cleaning_exclusions AS e
JOIN cleaning_log AS l ON l.rule_id = e.rule_id
JOIN molecules AS m ON m.chembl_id = e.record_id
WHERE e.dataset = 'molecules'
ORDER BY e.rule_id;

columns.name: dataset
columns.meaning: Which cleaned dataset the row belongs to: 'activities' (PDE4 measurements) or 'molecules' (inhaled vs oral analysis set).

columns.name: record_id
columns.meaning: ID of the excluded record: an activity_id for 'activities', a chembl_id for 'molecules'.

columns.name: rule_id
columns.meaning: Identifier of the cleaning rule: A = activities rules, M = molecules rules, followed by the order. Joins cleaning_log to cleaning_exclusions.
